decision: The Dayton Company enters discount merchandising through a separately named subsidiary, Target Stores, Inc.
state_before: department-store house plus a shopping-centre development arm; no discount operation
information_available: what the company later said it knew: that some shoppers want low margins and convenience; its own store-building capability
unknowns: every internal input: no memo, no study, no dissent, no rejected option survives
alternatives: UNKNOWN - no alternative is printed in any held layer, and a first public report printed three years later is not a deliberation record
constraints: private ownership of the parent; the format's capital appetite
rationale: the company's retrospective framing only: conceived with the knowledge that there also will be people who wish to take advantage of low margins and convenience shopping
expected_result: four stores operating by the close of 1962 as the company itself prints them
actual_result: UNKNOWN within the stage; the FY1965 print reports five stores and a 44 percent sales gain, which is the company's own account of the outcome

decision: Issue the company's first public annual report
information_available: projected growth; the option of staying private
unknowns: who argued for it, what was weighed, what the much deliberation consisted of
rationale: parent-level: projected growth requires it to expand beyond the concept of a privately-owned operation
expected_result: disclosure will further growth possibilities, open expansion opportunities, and put management under public scrutiny
actual_result: the first public stock offering followed in late 1967 (RESTATED by a 1971-dated report) and NYSE listing in 1969-09-08, both labeled RETROSPECTIVE and both outside this decision's own evidence

decision: Plan the first venture outside the Upper Midwest, at Denver, for Fall 1966
information_available: what the company printed as the test: dominance at home in a heavily-competitive metro
unknowns: whether any other candidate market was considered
constraints: capital and construction lead time implied by the interim financing note that follows
rationale: we believe the success of Target in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area provides an operational format which can do as well in other areas
expected_result: two stores opened in Denver in October 1966, total estate seven
actual_result: FY1967 prints that in their first full year the Denver stores matched the initial home performance - the company's own claim, no independent audit
